rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is no prior information about which modality, encoder, or fusion strategy is effective. The most fundamental uncertainty is whether either single modality alone provides a useful signal, and what performance floor we should expect. 2) What this tests: config_011 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50, no aggregation, no fusion) is the simplest possible configuration in the search space. It isolates the contribution of the image modality with a well-understood encoder and no additional complexity, establishing a clean single-modality baseline. 3) Why it is the best first experiment: Under a limited budget, establishing a clear performance floor with the fewest confounding design choices is the highest-information first step. It gives a reference point against which every subsequent multimodal or RNA-only experiment can be judged. If image-only performance is already strong, multimodal experiments must clear a high bar; if it is weak, it motivates exploring RNA or fusion. This simple anchor also makes later ablations (e.g., adding RNA, changing encoder, adding aggregation) interpretable because they differ from this baseline in exactly one dimension.

We have only one completed experiment (config_011: image_only, singleprofile, resnet50 → acc 0.208, F1 0.172), which is barely above chance, indicating the task is difficult or the current representation is insufficient. The most critical uncertainty right now is whether the low performance is due to a weak image encoder or a fundamental ceiling of the image modality. Config_039 (image_only, singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_011—only the image encoder changes from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L, holding profile setting, aggregation, and fusion constant. If ViT-L substantially outperforms ResNet50, we learn that representation quality is the bottleneck and should prioritize stronger encoders in multimodal settings. If it does not, we gain strong evidence that the image modality alone has a low ceiling and that RNA information (or multiprofile aggregation) is the more important axis to explore next. This experiment maximizes information gain per budget unit by isolating one key design variable without introducing confounds from modality, profile, or fusion changes.

We currently only have two image-only, singleprofile baselines (ResNet50: 0.208, ViT-L: 0.227), which establish that image alone yields modest performance and that ViT-L is the stronger image encoder. The most critical unresolved question is whether the RNA modality carries any predictive signal at all, since no RNA-only or multimodal result exists yet. config_045 (rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) is the cleanest parallel to our existing image-only singleprofile baselines: it isolates the RNA modality with the same profile setting and uses scgpt, the most expressive RNA encoder that appears in the multimodal configurations. This single experiment tells us (a) whether RNA has usable signal, (b) how it compares in magnitude to the image-only baselines, and (c) whether investing further experiments in multimodal fusion is warranted. It changes only the modality relative to our completed baselines, making the comparison direct and interpretable under a tight budget.

Evidence: RNA-only with scgpt (0.411 acc) substantially outperforms both image-only baselines (ResNet50: 0.208, ViT-L: 0.227), establishing RNA as the dominant modality. However, we have zero multimodal results, so the critical uncertainty is whether adding image information on top of the strong RNA signal provides any benefit. This experiment (config_017: multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) directly tests that question using the strongest known encoder for each modality while holding profile_setting=singleprofile to isolate the fusion effect. If it exceeds 0.411, multimodal fusion is validated and we can invest in exploring aggregation and multiprofile; if it does not, we know image adds little value and should focus on RNA encoder or profile improvements. This is the highest-information experiment under budget because the answer fundamentally redirects the remaining search.

Evidence: RNA-only with scgpt (config_045) achieves 0.411 acc, and adding image via weighted fusion (config_017) yields only a marginal gain to 0.422, indicating the RNA representation is the dominant performance driver. However, we have only tested one RNA encoder (scgpt), leaving critical uncertainty about whether the specific learned representation (scgpt's pretraining) or any decent RNA encoder would suffice. Question: config_049 (rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) isolates the RNA encoder variable with a single controlled change from config_045, testing whether a different learned representation (variational autoencoder, 200-dim) matches or diverges from scgpt. Why this is the best next experiment: Before investing budget in multiprofile aggregation, fusion strategy, or image encoder choices, we must understand whether the RNA encoder is a bottleneck or a flexible component. If scvi_n200 performs comparably to scgpt, the design space opens up (cheaper encoders, different fusion options); if it underperforms significantly, scgpt's pretraining is essential and we should focus optimization around it. This single-variable comparison maximizes information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_049 (scvi_n200, rna_only) achieved 0.520 acc, far outperforming config_045 (scgpt, rna_only) at 0.411. In multimodal, config_017 (scgpt + vit_l, weighted) gave only a marginal gain over scgpt alone (0.422 vs 0.411). The critical uncertainty is whether the image modality adds value when the RNA encoder is already strong (scvi_n200). This experiment (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, weighted, singleprofile) directly tests that question while keeping fusion and image encoder identical to config_017, isolating the RNA-encoder effect in the multimodal setting. If it substantially exceeds 0.520, multimodal with scvi_n200 is a promising direction to exploit; if it is near or below 0.520, we learn that image adds little and should redirect budget toward RNA-only multiprofile or aggregation experiments. This is the highest-information single step under the limited budget.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_036 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, weighted, singleprofile) at 0.537 acc, showing that scvi_n200 is a strong RNA encoder and weighted multimodal fusion provides a modest but consistent boost over RNA alone (0.520). However, the multiprofile dimension is completely untested—no experiment has yet explored whether aggregating multiple profiles improves performance. This is a high-uncertainty, high-impact design question. Question: config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) directly extends config_036 by changing only the profile setting from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of multiprofile while holding the best-known encoder and fusion choices constant. Why this experiment: It is the single most informative next step because (1) it builds on the strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + vit_l + weighted), (2) it tests the largest unexplored design axis, (3) avgpool is a simple, interpretable aggregation that cleanly answers 'does multiprofile help?' before committing budget to more complex aggregations like transformer, and (4) a positive result would open an entire new optimization space, while a null result would efficiently rule out multiprofile as a priority.

The strongest finding so far is the massive multiprofile gain: config_048 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, ViT-L, avgpool, weighted) reached 0.706 vs config_036 (same but singleprofile) at 0.537, a +0.169 jump. However, it is unclear whether this gain is driven by multiple RNA profiles, multiple image profiles, or the interaction. In the singleprofile setting, the image contributed only ~0.017 (config_036 vs config_049). Config_035 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean ablation that removes the image modality while preserving the multiprofile RNA pipeline and avgpool aggregation. If config_035 approaches ~0.70, the image adds little in the multiprofile regime and future effort should focus on RNA aggregation/fusion. If it drops substantially (e.g., below 0.60), the image profiles are a critical contributor and we should prioritize image-side design choices (aggregation, encoder). This single experiment isolates the image's marginal contribution in the multiprofile setting—the most important open question given the limited budget—without changing multiple variables simultaneously.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with avgpool/weighted (config_048, acc=0.706) is the best configuration, and the jump from singleprofile to multiprofile was the largest improvement observed (+0.17 over singleprofile multimodal). However, we have only tested avgpool aggregation in the multiprofile setting. The aggregation method is a critical design choice: avgpool treats all profiles symmetrically, while transformer can learn profile-specific attention and interactions. config_029 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer relative to config_048, making it a clean single-variable A/B test. This is the highest-value next experiment because it directly probes whether the current best configuration is bottlenecked by its aggregation strategy, and the result will determine whether further gains should be pursued through richer cross-profile modeling or through other dimensions (fusion, encoder choice).

The current best configuration (config_029: scvi_n200 + vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.725 accuracy. All top-performing multimodal experiments use 'weighted' fusion, but we have no evidence on whether 'concat' fusion could match or exceed it in this strong setting. Config_007 is identical to config_029 except for fusion (concat vs weighted), making it a clean single-variable A/B test. This is the best use of the next experiment because: (1) the evidence strongly supports the current backbone (scvi_n200, vit_l, multiprofile, transformer), so exploitation is warranted; (2) fusion strategy is the one design axis untested at the top of the performance hierarchy; (3) the result directly informs whether we should continue optimizing within the weighted-fusion family or pivot to concat-based architectures. No other available config isolates this question as cleanly.
